name: Poqomam, Eastern
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Santos Nicolas, Jose Francisco & Benito Perez, Jose Gonzalo. 1998. Rukorb'aal Poqom Q'orb'al: Gramatica Poqom (Poqomam). Cholsamaj. (entry merged into Poqomam poc)

new_statements.quote: En el idioma pocomam oriental no es necesario escribir el acento, porque éste siempre cae sobre la última sílaba de la palabra. Razón por la cual sus palabras son agudas, exceptuando algunas palabras prestadas del castellano; pues, éstas conservan el mismo acento que en el castellano. Vale la pena subrayar, que algunas palabras tomadas del castellano han adquirido la tonalidad y estilo del pocomam. Un ejemplo claro de ésto son las siguientes tres palabras graves: camixa – camisa; patu' – pato; luara' – loro.
new_statements.translation: In the Eastern Pocomam language it is not necessary to write the accent, because it always falls on the last syllable of the word. For this reason its words are oxytone (agudas), except for some words borrowed from Spanish, since these keep the same accent as in Spanish. It is worth underlining that some words taken from Spanish have acquired the tonality and style of Pocomam. A clear example of this are the following three paroxytone (graves) words: camixa 'shirt' (camisa); patu' 'duck' (pato); luara' 'parrot' (loro).
new_statements.citation: McArthur, Carolina de & Ricardo McArthur (compilers). 1995. Diccionario pocomam y español. Guatemala: Instituto Lingüístico de Verano de Centroamérica. xxiv+234 pp. [Eastern Poqomam of San Luis Jilotepeque, Jalapa; SIL Language & Culture Archives entry 26288; Glottolog ref 90276]. Same wording first in McArthur, Carol & Richard McArthur. 1983. Aprendamos pocomam, en pocomam oriental y español. Guatemala: ILV, p. ix.
new_statements.locator: 'Instrucciones para su uso', section 'Ortografía', p. xix (PDF p. 22 of the SIL scan); identical passage in Aprendamos pocomam (1983), 'El alfabeto pocomam', p. ix (PDF p. 11)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Independent check. (1) Quote: I re-rendered PDF p. 22 of myself (page render, 100 dpi) and read it by eye; it is printed p. xix, running head 'Instrucciones para su uso'. The passage is there exactly as quoted: 'En el idioma pocomam oriental no es necesario escribir el acento, porque éste siempre cae sobre la última sílaba de la palabra. Razón por la cual sus palabras son agudas, exceptuando algunas palabras prestadas del castellano; pues, éstas conservan el mismo acento que en el castellano. Vale la pena subrayar, que algunas palabras tomadas del castellano han adquirido la tonalidad y estilo del pocomam. Un ejemplo claro de ésto son las siguientes tres palabras graves:' followed by a boxe…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is fixed on the final syllable of every native word (hence not written in the orthography). Spanish loanwords, even ones phonologically nativized (x for s, final glottal stop), keep their Spanish (here penultimate) stress.
new_statements.exceptions: Spanish loans keep Spanish stress; the three nativized loans camixa, patu', luara' are explicitly labelled 'palabras graves' (penult-stressed).
new_statements.domain_note: Word level ('la última sílaba de la palabra'); stated as an orthographic-pronunciation note in a dictionary / language primer, not an instrumental or phrase-level study. Source is SIL missionary-linguist work (based on Raymond Zinn's 1964-68 fieldwork), Eastern dialect of San Luis Jilotepeque only.
new_statements.identity_note: poqo1257 is a Glottolog bookkeeping languoid for the retired ISO code [poa] 'Eastern Pokomam', merged into Poqomam [poc] (Glottolog poqo1253) by ISO 639-3 CR 2008-057 (adopted 2009-01-16; held file). The deciding source (McArthur & McArthur 1995) is the one Glottolog itself attaches to poqo1257 and states on p. xiii that it 'refleja el idioma pocomam que se habla en el municipio de San Luis Jilotepeque' (dept. Jalapa) and does NOT represent San Pedro Pinula, Chinautla, Mixco or Palín; it rests on Raymond Zinn's SIL fieldwork in San Luis Jilotepeque 1964-68. So the statement is specific to the Eastern (Jilotepeque) dialect. The same wording appears in the authors' 1983 primer Aprendamos pocomam (p. ix), also Eastern. The catalog entry for Poqomam as a whole (poqo1253) currently rests only on family-level surveys; this first-hand Eastern-dialect statement could serve it too, with the dialect noted.
